original_target.title: Gaussian fluctuations of the optimal Euclidean traveling-salesman tour

full_original_statement: Let $`X_1,X_2,\ldots`$ be independent uniform points in $`[0,1]^2`$. Let $`L_n`$ be the minimum Euclidean length of a closed polygonal tour visiting $`X_1,\ldots,X_n`$. Does $`(L_n-\mathbb E L_n)/\sqrt{\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}\nolimits(L_n)}`$ converge in distribution to the standard normal law as $`n\to\infty`$? The tour must be globally optimal; a tour produced by a specified heuristic is not substituted for $`L_n`$.
